title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, and the Ministry of Public Security on Issuing the Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases of Infringement of Intellectual Property Rights
keywords_en: Intellectual property; Criminal cases concerning infringement of intellectual property rights
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court  Supreme People's Procuratorate  Ministry of Public Security

Notice on Issuing the Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases of Intellectual Property Infringement

Fa Fa [2011] No. 3

The Higher People's Courts, People's Procuratorates, and Public Security Departments (Bureaus) of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army, the Military Procuratorate of the People's Liberation Army, and the Security Department of the General Political Department; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; and the People's Procuratorate and Public Security Bureau of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:

In order to address the new situations and new problems encountered by public security organs, people's procuratorates, and people's courts in handling criminal cases of intellectual property infringement in recent years, to punish criminal activities of intellectual property infringement according to law, and to maintain the order of the socialist market economy, the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, and the Ministry of Public Security, on the basis of in-depth investigation and research and extensive solicitation of opinions from all parties, have formulated the Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases of Intellectual Property Infringement. These are hereby issued to you. Please organize serious study and ensure their implementation. For important issues encountered during implementation, please promptly report them level by level to the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, and the Ministry of Public Security.

January 10, 2011

Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases of Intellectual Property Infringement

In order to address the new situations and new problems encountered by public security organs, people's procuratorates, and people's courts in handling criminal cases of intellectual property infringement in recent years, to punish criminal activities of intellectual property infringement according to law, and to maintain the order of the socialist market economy, these Opinions are formulated in accordance with the Criminal Law, the Criminal Procedure Law, and relevant judicial interpretations, combined with the practice of investigation, prosecution, and adjudication.

I. Issues concerning the jurisdiction over cases of intellectual property infringement crimes

Cases of intellectual property infringement crimes shall be placed on file for investigation by the public security organ at the place where the crime was committed. When necessary, the public security organ at the place where the criminal suspect resides may place the case on file for investigation. The place where the crime was committed in cases of intellectual property infringement crimes includes the place where the infringing products are manufactured, stored, transported, or sold; the location of the server of the website disseminating infringing works or selling infringing products, the place of network access, the place where the website establisher or manager is located; the place where the uploader of the infringing works is located; and the place where the harmful result of the crime occurs and the rights holder actually suffers harm. Where there are multiple places where the crime was committed for intellectual property infringement, jurisdiction shall be vested in the public security organ that first accepted the case or the public security organ at the main place where the crime was committed. If public security organs at multiple places where the crime was committed have a dispute over jurisdiction, the common superior public security organ shall designate jurisdiction. Where requests for approval of arrest, transfer for review and prosecution, or initiation of public prosecution are required, the case shall be accepted by the people's procuratorate and the people's court at the same level as the public security organ.

For intellectual property infringement acts, such as the manufacture, storage, transportation, or sale of the same batch of infringing products, committed across regions by different criminal suspects or criminal groups, where the conditions for consolidated handling are met, the relevant public security organs may jointly place the case on file for investigation. Where requests for approval of arrest, transfer for review and prosecution, or initiation of public prosecution are required, the case shall be accepted by the people's procuratorate and the people's court at the same level as the public security organ.

II. Issues concerning the validity of evidence collected or obtained by administrative law enforcement departments in handling criminal cases of intellectual property infringement

Physical evidence, documentary evidence, audio-visual materials, inspection reports, expert conclusions, inspection records, and on-site records lawfully collected, obtained, or made by administrative law enforcement departments may be used as criminal evidence after being examined by the public security organ or the people's procuratorate and confirmed through cross-examination during court proceedings by the people's court.

For witness testimony, statements of the parties, and other investigation records made by administrative law enforcement departments, if the public security organ deems it necessary to use them as criminal evidence, it shall lawfully re-collect or re-make them.

III. Issues concerning sampling for evidence and commissioning expert evaluations in handling criminal cases of intellectual property infringement

When handling criminal cases of intellectual property infringement, the public security organ may, based on work needs, conduct sampling for evidence or consult with the administrative law enforcement department at the same level or relevant inspection institutions to assist in sampling. Where laws or regulations have provisions on the sampling institution or sampling method, the mandated institution shall be commissioned and samples shall be extracted in accordance with the prescribed method.

When handling criminal cases of intellectual property infringement, the public security organ, the people's procuratorate, and the people's court shall, for matters requiring expert evaluation, commission a nationally recognized expert evaluation institution with the relevant qualifications to conduct the evaluation.

The public security organ, the people's procuratorate, and the people's court shall review the expert conclusions, hear the opinions of the rights holder, the criminal suspect, and the defendant on the expert conclusions, and may request the expert evaluation institution to provide corresponding explanations.

IV. Issues concerning the collection of evidence in private prosecution cases of intellectual property infringement crimes

For a private prosecution case of intellectual property infringement lawfully accepted by the people's court, if the party is unable to obtain evidence due to objective reasons but can provide relevant leads when initiating the private prosecution and apply to the people's court for collection, the people's court shall collect the evidence according to law.

V. Issues concerning the determination of "identical goods" as provided in Article 213 of the Criminal Law

Goods with the same name and goods with different names that refer to the same thing may be determined as "identical goods." "Name" refers to the name used for goods by the Trademark Office of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce in trademark registration work, usually the name of goods specified in the International Classification of Goods and Services for the Purposes of the Registration of Marks. "Goods with different names that refer to the same thing" means goods that are the same or substantially the same in terms of function, purpose, main raw materials, consumers, and sales channels, and that the relevant public generally considers to be the same type of goods.

The determination of "identical goods" shall be made by comparing the goods designated for use in the rights holder's registered trademark with the goods actually produced and sold by the actor.

VI. Issues concerning the determination of "a trademark that is identical to its registered trademark" as provided in Article 213 of the Criminal Law

Any of the following circumstances may be determined as "a trademark that is identical to its registered trademark":

(1) Changing the font, letter case, or horizontal or vertical arrangement of the characters of the registered trademark, with only minor differences from the registered trademark;

(2) Changing the spacing between characters, letters, numbers, etc., of the registered trademark, without affecting the reflection of the distinctive features of the registered trademark;

(3) Changing the color of the registered trademark;

(4) Other trademarks that are visually substantially indistinguishable from the registered trademark and sufficient to mislead the public.

VII. Issues concerning whether the value of infringing products that have not yet been affixed or fully affixed with counterfeit registered trademark labels should be included in the amount of illegal business operations

When calculating the value of counterfeit registered trademark infringing products that have been manufactured, stored, transported, or not yet sold, if there is reliable and sufficient evidence that products that have been completed but not yet affixed (including pasted) or not yet fully affixed (including pasted) with counterfeit registered trademark labels will be used to counterfeit another person's registered trademark, their value shall be included in the amount of illegal business operations.

VIII. Issues concerning conviction and sentencing in cases of selling goods bearing counterfeit registered trademarks where the goods have not yet been sold or have been partially sold

Whoever sells goods that they know bear counterfeit registered trademarks, under any of the following circumstances, shall be convicted and punished for the crime of selling goods bearing counterfeit registered trademarks (attempted) in accordance with Article 214 of the Criminal Law:

(1) The goods bearing counterfeit registered trademarks have not yet been sold, and the value of the goods is RMB 150,000 or more;

(2) The goods bearing counterfeit registered trademarks have been partially sold, the amount of sales is less than RMB 50,000, but the total value of the goods bearing counterfeit registered trademarks that have been sold and those not yet sold is RMB 150,000 or more.

If the goods bearing counterfeit registered trademarks have not yet been sold, and their value reaches RMB 150,000 or more but less than RMB 250,000, or RMB 250,000 or more, the actor shall be convicted and punished according to the respective statutory sentencing ranges provided in Article 214 of the Criminal Law.

If the sales amount and the value of unsold goods reach different statutory sentencing ranges or both reach the same statutory sentencing range, the punishment shall be imposed within the heavier statutory sentencing range or the same statutory sentencing range, with a heavier penalty at discretion.

IX. Issues concerning conviction in cases of selling illegally manufactured registered trademark labels where the labels have not yet been sold or have been partially sold

Whoever sells another person's forged or unauthorized manufactured registered trademark labels, under any of the following circumstances, shall be convicted and punished for the crime of selling illegally manufactured registered trademark labels (attempted) in accordance with Article 215 of the Criminal Law:

(1) The quantity of another person's forged or unauthorized manufactured registered trademark labels that have not yet been sold is 60,000 pieces or more;

(2) The quantity of two or more types of another person's forged or unauthorized manufactured registered trademark labels that have not yet been sold is 30,000 pieces or more;

(3) The labels of another person's forged or unauthorized manufactured registered trademark have been partially sold, the quantity sold is less than 20,000 pieces, but the total quantity of labels sold and unsold is 60,000 pieces or more;

(4) Two or more types of another person's forged or unauthorized manufactured registered trademark labels have been partially sold, the quantity sold is less than 10,000 pieces, but the total quantity of labels sold and unsold is 30,000 pieces or more.

X. Issues concerning the determination of "for the purpose of profit" in cases of copyright infringement crimes

Except for sales, any of the following circumstances may be determined as "for the purpose of profit":

(1) Directly or indirectly collecting fees by publishing paid advertisements in another person's work, bundling a third party's work, or other means;

(2) Disseminating another person's work through an information network, or using infringing works uploaded by others to provide paid advertisement publishing services on a website or webpage, directly or indirectly collecting fees;

(3) Disseminating another person's work through an information network on a membership basis, collecting membership registration fees or other fees;

(4) Other circumstances of utilizing another person's work for profit.

XI. Issues concerning the determination of "without the permission of the copyright owner" in cases of copyright infringement crimes

"Without the permission of the copyright owner" shall generally be determined based on the copyright certification document for the work in question issued by the copyright owner or its authorized agent, the collective management organization of copyright, or the copyright certification institution designated by the national copyright administrative department, or based on evidence proving that the publisher or the person who reproduced or distributed the work forged or altered the authorization license document or exceeded the scope of the authorization license, combined with other evidence.

In cases where there are many types of works involved and the rights holders are scattered, if it is truly difficult to obtain the above evidence one by one, but there is evidence proving that the reproductions in question were illegally published, reproduced, or distributed, and the publisher or the person who reproduced or distributed the work cannot provide relevant materials proving that they obtained the permission of the copyright owner, it may be determined as "without the permission of the copyright owner." However, this does not apply if there is evidence proving that the rights holder has waived their rights, the copyright of the work in question is not protected by the Copyright Law of the PRC, or the term of copyright protection has expired.

XII. Issues concerning the determination of "distribution" as provided in Article 217 of the Criminal Law and related issues

"Distribution" includes general distribution, wholesale, retail, dissemination through information networks, rental, exhibition and sale, and other activities.

Illegally publishing, reproducing, or distributing another person's work, infringing copyright and constituting a crime, shall be convicted and punished as the crime of copyright infringement, and shall not be determined as other crimes such as the crime of illegal business operations.

XIII. Issues concerning the standards for conviction and punishment for acts of disseminating infringing works through information networks

Whoever, for the purpose of profit, without the permission of the copyright owner, disseminates to the public through an information network another person's literary works, musical works, cinematographic works, television works, works of fine art, photographic works, audiovisual works, sound recordings or video recordings, computer software, or other works, under any of the following circumstances, shall be considered as having "other serious circumstances" as provided in Article 217 of the Criminal Law:

(1) The amount of illegal business operations is RMB 50,000 or more;

(2) The total number of copies of another person's works disseminated is 500 (copies/parts) or more;

(3) The actual number of clicks on another person's works disseminated reaches 50,000 or more;

(4) Disseminating another person's works through an information network on a membership basis, with registered members reaching 1,000 or more;

(5) Where the amount or quantity does not meet the standards set out in subparagraphs (1) to (4), but reaches more than half of the standards set out in any two or more of those subparagraphs;

(6) Other circumstances of serious nature.

If, in committing the acts provided in the preceding paragraph, the amount or quantity reaches five times or more the standards set out in subparagraphs (1) to (5) of the preceding paragraph, it shall be considered as "other particularly serious circumstances" as provided in Article 217 of the Criminal Law.

XIV. Issues concerning the cumulative calculation of amounts for multiple acts of intellectual property infringement

In accordance with the provisions of Article 12, paragraph 2, of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases of Intellectual Property Infringement, where multiple acts of intellectual property infringement have been committed without being subject to administrative or criminal punishment, the amount of illegal business operations, the amount of illegal gains, or the sales amount shall be calculated cumulatively.

If a person commits multiple unlawful acts of intellectual property infringement within two years, without being subject to administrative punishment, and the cumulative amount constitutes a crime, they shall be convicted and punished according to law. The statute of limitations for prosecuting acts of intellectual property infringement crimes shall be governed by the relevant provisions of the Criminal Law and shall not be limited by the aforementioned two-year period.

XV. Issues concerning the characterization of acts providing raw materials, mechanical equipment, etc., for others to commit intellectual property infringement crimes

Whoever, knowing that another person is committing an intellectual property infringement crime, provides assistance such as the main raw materials, auxiliary materials, semi-finished products, packaging materials, mechanical equipment, labels or marks, production technology, or formulas for the production or manufacture of infringing products, or provides services such as internet access, server hosting, network storage space, communication transmission channels, fee collection, or settlement of accounts, shall be dealt with as an accomplice to the intellectual property infringement crime.

XVI. Issues concerning the handling of concurrent offenses of intellectual property infringement crimes

If an actor commits an intellectual property infringement crime, and the act also constitutes a crime of producing or selling counterfeit or substandard goods, the actor shall be convicted and punished according to the provisions that impose a heavier penalty among the intellectual property infringement crime and the crime of producing or selling counterfeit or substandard goods.
